goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:17 — Removing both header floats without a non-flex fallback stacks or overlaps the logo and panel in supported IE9, which ignores every display value emitted by flexbox().

app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:17 — The new nowrap flex row leaves the attacker-controlled .extra-info-wrapper at min-width:auto, so an unbreakable topic title can push the ordered panel and all header controls off-screen.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows .contents getting flexbox() applied (line 17-18 in header.scss), and .extra-info-wrapper getting order(2) in topic.scss. The finding correctly identifies that without explicit min-width or overflow handling on flex children, a long unbreakable string in .extra-info-wrapper could push other flex items (like .panel with order(3)) off-screen. This is a known flexbox behavior where min-width:auto is the default. The diff doesn't show any min-width:0 or overflow handling being added to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:118 — flexbox() advertises the -moz-box fallback but align-items() omits -moz-box-align, so Firefox 21 and earlier silently use stretch instead of the requested center or baseline alignment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows flexbox() mixin includes -moz-box display fallback for older Firefox, but align-items() mixin at lines 115-120 only includes -webkit-box-align, -webkit-align-items, -ms-flex-align, -ms-align-items, and align-items - it's missing -moz-box-align. This is an inconsistency where the display fallback is provided but the corresponding alignment property fallback is omitted, which could cause alignment issues in Firefox 21 and earlier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:263 — The flex conversion leaves `.small-action-desc` non-growing, so its existing right-floated action button no longer anchors to the row's right edge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `.small-action` is converted to flexbox (lines 264-266), but `.small-action-desc` only has padding changes without any flex-grow or margin-left:auto properties added. In the original float-based layout, elements could float right within the container. With flexbox, without explicit flex-grow or margin properties on `.small-action-desc`, any right-floated action buttons inside would no longer anchor to the right edge of the row. This is a legitimate layout concern that could break the visual appearance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117 — The alignment mixin omits `-moz-box-align`, so the newly added center and baseline alignment is lost in legacy Firefox despite explicitly selecting its `-moz-box` flex mode.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the @mixin align-items() at lines 117-123 includes -webkit-box-align, -webkit-align-items, -ms-flex-align, -ms-align-items, and align-items, but does NOT include -moz-box-align. Meanwhile, the @mixin flexbox() at lines 97-103 includes 'display: -moz-box' for legacy Firefox support. This is inconsistent - the code enables -moz-box display mode but doesn't provide the corresponding -moz-box-align property for alignment, meaning alignment won't work in legacy Firefox browsers that use the -moz-box flex model.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:264 — Multi-line custom small actions are not covered despite changed centering and spacing, so tall messages can become vertically misaligned or compressed unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that .small-action now uses flexbox with align-items(center), and .small-action-desc has changed padding from '0.5em 0 0.5em 4em' to '0 1.5%' with margin-top removed. The nested p element also has margin changed from '5px 0' to '0'. These changes affect vertical spacing and alignment. The finding raises a valid concern that multi-line content within small actions may not render correctly with the new centered flexbox layout, as the vertical centering could cause issues with taller content. This is a legitimate edge case concern about the CSS changes, though it's not definitively a bug without visual testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:100 — The new legacy-prefixed flex output has no cross-browser layout coverage, leaving the header ordering and right-alignment behavior at risk on the older engines these prefixes target.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the flexbox mixins have 'no cross-browser layout coverage', but examining the diff shows the mixins include comprehensive vendor prefixes: -webkit-box, -moz-box, -ms-flexbox, -webkit-flex for flexbox(); similar coverage for inline-flex(), align-items(), and order(). The mixins actually provide extensive legacy browser support. The claim that there's 'no cross-browser layout coverage' is factually incorrect based on what the diff shows.
